entries.jsdocSummary: The feature's oRPC entrypoint: its contract, and the router built from one factory per procedure. The whole tree lives in one `entrypoints/procedures.ts`; each leaf takes the feature's `rpcImplementer` as a typed parameter, so it never imports the feature at runtime. The contract stays the one list of procedure names: a missing, extra or wrong procedure does not compile. `DefinedFeature.contract` / `.router` are read from this descriptor, so `routerFor(rpcContract, features)` finds the feature by its contract. Its actions (one per procedure, `<feature>.<path>`) are named when the feature compiles, through `actionsOf`. A subtree whose built router IS a declared child's router is the child's: the child names those actions itself, so they are skipped here. An inline group (`admin: impl => ({ … })`) has no child owner and keeps its actions.
